sections.title: The Foundation for Large Models
sections.body: Training modern LLMs and generative models requires two things: immense compute power and low-latency interconnects. Kenya AI Compute provides both. Our GPU clusters are built on high-bandwidth Spine-Leaf architecture, ensuring that data flows freely between nodes during large-scale distributed training runs. We offer a mix of NVIDIA A100 (40GB/80GB) and H100 units, as well as AMD Instinct alternatives, allowing you to choose the price-to-performance ratio that fits your R&D budget. By taking advantage of our Kenyan energy arbitrage, we can offer reserved training instances at up to 50% less than standard cloud providers, enabling researchers to run longer experiments and train larger models for the same capital outlay. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models. sections.title: Training Capabilities
items: Hardware: H100 80GB and A100 80GB clusters with NVLink support.
Networking: RDMA-enabled 100G/400G internal fabric for sync-heavy training.
Software: Pre-installed PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX with optimized CUDA drivers.
Storage: Local NVMe scratch space for fast checkpointing.
Pricing: On-demand from $1.00/GPU-hour, with deep discounts for reserved terms.
